name: application-keyboard-shortcut-cheatsheet
title: Keyboard Shortcut Cheatsheet
description: Modal dialog listing every keyboard shortcut grouped under headings (General, Editing, Navigation, View), conventionally opened with the "?" key.
useWhen: Your application has enough keyboard shortcuts that they need a discoverable, grouped reference.
You want a conventional "?" trigger that power users already expect from apps like Linear, Superhuman, and GitHub.
Pairing with a Command Palette so users can discover shortcuts for actions they already found by search.
avoidWhen: You only have two or three shortcuts — an inline Kbd hint next to each action is enough, a full modal is unnecessary.
The list needs to be searchable or filterable — this is a static reference grid, not a search UI.
responsiveBehavior: The shortcut groups render in a 2-column grid at the dialog's max width; collapse to a single column on narrow viewports so labels and keys don't compress.
accessibility: The dialog carries role="dialog" and aria-modal="true", with aria-labelledby pointing at the visible title.
Escape closes the dialog; clicking the backdrop also closes it, while clicking inside the panel does not.
Key glyphs use the native <kbd> element so assistive technology recognizes them as keyboard input.
Every shortcut pairs a text label with its keys so meaning never depends on the key glyph alone.

variants.title: Keyboard Shortcut Cheatsheet
variants.description: A four-group shortcut reference (General, Editing, Navigation, View) in a 2-column grid, with a footer hint about the "?" trigger.
accessibility: Focus should move into the dialog on open and return to the trigger on close in a full implementation.

variants.title: Keyboard Shortcut Cheatsheet (Dark)
variants.description: The same four-group shortcut reference adapted for dark surfaces.
accessibility: Backdrop and panel contrast remain distinguishable against dark page content.
